title: OpenAI Employees Pocket $6.6B in Historic Share Sale
excerpt: More than 600 current and former staff cashed out stock in October 2025, averaging $11M each — before any IPO.
body:
Over 600 OpenAI employees quietly became millionaires last October, and the world is only now taking note. In one of the largest pre-IPO employee stock sales in tech history, current and former staff collectively sold $6.6 billion worth of shares through a structured tender offer, averaging roughly $11 million per person.

**What happened — the details of the deal:**
The secondary sale took place in October 2025, with investors including Thrive Capital, SoftBank, Dragoneer, MGX, and T. Rowe Price buying the shares. OpenAI tripled the individual selling cap from $10 million to $30 million, and approximately 75 employees hit that ceiling — meaning at least $2.25 billion flowed to that small group alone. Employees who joined when OpenAI first issued shares seven years ago saw their equity grow more than 100-fold, a return that dwarfed even the Nasdaq composite's performance over the same period.

**Why this matters — the AI talent war in plain sight:**
The deal did not involve new shares; OpenAI raised no fresh capital. Instead, it gave long-tenured staff a rare chance to convert paper wealth into real money without waiting for a public listing. The move is a direct response to fierce competition for AI talent — Meta has reportedly dangled compensation packages approaching $300 million to lure elite researchers away. Secondary sales are now Silicon Valley's preferred pressure valve, letting firms like OpenAI, SpaceX, and Stripe reward loyalty while staying private longer.

**What to watch — the IPO countdown:**
OpenAI, now valued at $852 billion after a March 2026 funding round, is preparing for a potential public offering later this year — a listing that would unlock liquidity for thousands more employees and reshape the AI investment landscape entirely.
nri_angle: Indian-American engineers and researchers are among the most prominent workers in OpenAI's workforce, making this wealth-creation event directly relevant to the community's growing footprint at the frontier of AI.
